utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-99-36/2-I, the Prosecutor versus Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: So this is the Further Initial Appearance of Stojan Zupljanin pursuant to Rule 62 of the Rules. At the initial appearance held on 23 June, 2008, the accused, Stojan Zupljanin, decided to avail himself of the right to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty within 30 days of his Initial Appearance. The 30-day time limit is about to expire, and the accused has the opportunity to enter a plea at today's sitting. But first, Mr. Zupljanin, can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear, Mr. Stole, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: May I have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon. My name is Anna Richterova, and I'm accompanied by Karen Beausey and case manager Crispian Smith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence for Mr. Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. I am Tomislav Visnjic, attorney-at-law, and I'm going to be representing Mr. Zupljanin today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. I shall recall from the Initial Appearance that you, Mr. Zupljanin, are the only accused in the indictment with case number IT-99-36-I, confirmed by Judge Rodrigues on 17 December, 1999, and made public on 13 July, 2001. This indictment was afterwards amended under Second Amended Indictment in 6th October 2004 is the operative indictment in the present case. I will now proceed with the procedural part of the Further Initial Appearance of the accused, Mr. Zupljanin, pursuant to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. First, Mr. Zupljanin, have you received the indictment in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Have you read the indictment and understood its contents?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have read it and understood the contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: As mentioned also the last time, you have a right to have the indictment read out in full. As also mentioned the last time, you can waive that right and state that the summary provided to you already is sufficient. In this case, we will proceed with the charges against you. Do you wish to have the indictment read out in full or do you waive this right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stole, on this occasion I wish to say, and I will continue saying this throughout the proceedings, that I am truly unhappy that the war ever came to the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Had I been able to prevent it, there would have been no war, for certain. It is necessary for all of us to learn a lesson once again, aware of the fact that we can and need to live with each other as human beings, without desire for revenge or ambitions for domination; and I will be happy if my sacrifice is the last sacrifice in that territory. Could more have been done --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Mr. Zupljanin, the question was now if you wanted to have the indictment read out in full or if you waive that right, and then we will proceed to the charges.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In essence, Mr. Stole, I truly want the entire proceedings to be carried out for historic truth and re-establishment of trust, and I wish to say that I'm not guilty and there is no need to read out the text that you wanted us to read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. The next step of this appearance is, then, that I will ask you if you are ready to enter a plea or to plead to all or any of the counts of the indictment brought against you. And the first possibility is then for you to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty to each of the 12 counts you are charged with in the indictment. And if you desire not to enter a plea to these counts, I shall enter a plea of not guilty on your behalf. Are you prepared, Mr. Zupljanin, to enter a plea to the charges against you, and can we proceed to that now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am prepared, Mr. Stole, and I hereby state that I'm not guilty with respect to all counts of indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: I understand that we have to do this in more detail. That's the procedure of the Rules. In relation to each charge, I will ask you, how do you plead to that charge, guilty or not guilty, and your answer in each case should be, "Guilty," or, "Not guilty," as the case may be. You should bear in mind that you are charged with both Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 7(3), of the Statutes, command responsibility for all counts. Mr. Zupljanin, will you please stand up. The first count you are charged is a charge of persecutions on political, racial and religious grounds, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(H) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: The second count you are charged with is the charge of extermination, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(B) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: The third count with which you are charged is a charge of murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(A) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: The fourth count with which you are charged is the charge of murder in violation of the laws of customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: The fifth count with which you are charged is a charge of torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(F) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: The sixth count with which you are charged is the charge of torture, a violation of the Laws or Customs of War, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: The seventh count with which you are charged is a charge of cruel treatment, a violation of the Laws and Customs of War, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: The eighth count with which you are charged is the charge of inhumane acts, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(I) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: The ninth count with which you are charged is a charge of deportation, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(D) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: The 10th charge with which you are charged is the charge of inhumane acts, forcible transfer, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(I) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: The 11th count with which you are charged is a charge of wanton destruction or devastation of towns or villages not justified by military necessity, a violation of the Laws or Customs of War, punishable under Article 3(B) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: And the 12th and last count with which you are charged is the charge of destruction or willful damage done to institutions dedicated to religion, a violation of the Laws or Customs of War, punishable under Article 3(D) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: I would like to ask the Registrar to note that Mr. Zupljanin has pleaded not guilty to all counts of the indictment. I would also like to inform you, Mr. Zupljanin, that according to Rule 62 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, you may charge your plea of not guilty to a guilty plea in relation to some or all counts at a later stage. I just inform you of that right. Mr. Zupljanin, you may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: As regard the further proceedings, the Registrar will at a point set a date for trial. A status conference will be scheduled within 120 days of this appearance, and the purpose of the status conference is two-fold. First, it is to organise exchanges between the parties and facilitate expeditious preparation for trial. Second, the Pre-Trial Judge will have an opportunity to see you in person to ensure that you are being treated well and to be made aware of any complaints or requests that you may have. You will be informed of the exact date of the status conference in due course. At the Initial Appearance, the Prosecutor undertook, in accordance with Rule 66(A)(i) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence to make available to the permanent defence counsel for the accused the supporting material which accompanied the indictment, has the Prosecution done so?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the Prosecution has disclosed the supporting material. However, we did not disclose one statement because of a witness who has been granted protective measure of delayed disclosure in previous proceedings, and on 10th of July, 2008, the Prosecution filed a motion for protective measures for victims and witnesses and notification of protective measures in force, in which the name of the witness is mentioned in ex parte.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Defence counsel, I take it, can confirm what has just been stated, and you will perhaps also confirm that you will be commenting on this motion in due time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. I hereby confirm that disclosure was partially carried out pursuant to Rule 66; and I also confirm that we will also submit our response to the Prosecution motions for provisional measures and the other one for the joinder, and later on would you please give me the opportunity to address you again on that same issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. In fact, that is now the -- or there is one more thing, but I know that Mr. Visnjic is an experienced counsel, and I do not have to enlighten him on the Rules of Procedure of this Tribunal, here under Rule 72(A) and the 30-day period for filing preliminary motions, once you have received the supporting material. Is there, then, at this stage any matter that the Prosecution wishes to raise?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There is nothing which we would like to raise at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I wanted to address you pursuant to the deadline under Rule 72(A) for preliminary motions concerning the indictment. As you are well aware, on the 15th of July, 2008, the Prosecution filed a motion to join the two cases, Stanisic and Zupljanin, and at the same time they asked for leave to amend the indictment. I hereby express an oral motion to extend the deadline for Mr. Zupljanin for preliminary motions concerning the indictment, in view of the possible rulings of the Trial Chamber. Should the cases Zupljanin and Stanisic not be joined, we would ask for a deadline of 30 days under Rule 72(A) to start running from the date of the ruling on the joinder motion or from the date of the disclosure of the entire supportive material, unless the Prosecution completes this prior to the issuance of the Court ruling. Should the cases Zupljanin and Stanisic be joined, we would ask for a deadline of 30 days from the moment of completion of entire supporting material for the new indictment, disclosure of that material, since we support that this new indictment would have a somewhat different supporting material than the existing one. If we were to uphold the current deadline, in view of the current indictment against Mr. Zupljanin, we would come into a difficult situation where the Court would be acting on the basis of one indictment and, in the meantime, a ruling on the amended indictment would be passed, which would put Mr. Zupljanin into a legally insufficiently-defined situation where it would not be clear to him against which indictment he needs to defend himself. Therefore, I hereby request that the Trial Chamber grant us a different or a new deadline for our response under Rule 72(A), in line with what I have just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution want to comment on these observations by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do not object, and we consider it a reasonable amount of time for the response. Moreover, in our motion, in the part 6 relief sought, we propose that the lead counsel file his initial submission after the motion according to Rule 92 bis -- sorry, according to 72 is decided or has been decided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. So the parties seem to be, then, in agreement about this, that this seems to be the sensible thing to do under the circumstances; and on that basis this oral motion will be granted. I don't know if this is sufficient to just state for the record here and now. If there would be any need to later clarify this in writing, we will do so; but as I said, this motion will then be granted for the extension of time, as requested by the Defence for Mr. Zupljanin. Is there, then, anything else we have to deal with at this point in time? Not from the Prosecution, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No, there is nothing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: And from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Not for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any matter that the accused wishes to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stole, I just wanted to say two sentences, if I may. When it comes to my Defence team, for a while I considered defending myself, but in the meantime I have decided to appoint Mr. Visnjic as my counsel. However, I wish to add that I want to participate actively in my Defence, and I will inform you on the mode of my participation once I complete my Defence team. I also wish to congratulate my son, Mladen, and wish him a happy birthday, and also to my other son whose birthday was on Friday, and I didn't have an opportunity to wish him a happy birthday. My other son's name is Pavle. I also would like to ask that I be given a computer by the Detention Unit. I expect that I will need a computer fairly soon, and I submitted a timely request. Therefore, I ask that you put in a plea on my behalf to have this resolved as speedily as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: As for the request for a computer, I suggest that you take this with your counsel and with the Detention Unit. That would be the way to go about for the thing you raised there. And, of course, for what role you will wish to take with counsel, assisted by counsel, would be to a certain extent, at least, for the two of you to confer or to consult about, to a certain extent. I leave it at that for now, and as there is no other business at this time, these proceedings are adjourned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.25 p.m.
